q: A lifter adds a little more weight to the bar each week so the muscles keep adapting. Which training principle is this?
e: Gradually raising the load is progressive overload.

q: A swimmer trains only in the pool and finds that her running endurance barely improves. Which principle explains this?
o: Specificity: the body adapts to the type of training done
e: Training effects are specific to the activity.

q: Using a longer lever, such as a straight arm, makes a throw travel faster at the hand. What biomechanical idea is this?
o: Longer levers can produce greater speed at the end
e: A longer lever moves its tip faster for the same rotation.

q: A sprinter pushes backward against the track and moves forward. Which law of motion describes this?
o: Newton's third law: every action has an equal and opposite reaction
e: Pushing back on the ground drives the body forward.

q: Before a workout on a weight machine, which safety step should you take first?
o: Check that the pin and seat are set correctly
e: Checking equipment prevents injuries.

q: Why should a spotter be used on a heavy bench press?
o: To help if the lifter cannot finish a repetition
e: A spotter keeps the lifter safe.

q: A student practices a jump rope skill ten minutes a day for two weeks and gets smoother. This shows that skills improve with what?
e: Deliberate practice improves performance.

q: Which practice habit best improves a skill during fitness activities?
o: Repeating the movement with correct form and getting feedback
e: Correct repetition builds skill.

q: A student performs a basic squat with feet shoulder-width apart and knees tracking over the toes. This shows competency in what?
o: Using the proper technique for a basic exercise
e: Basic competency means correct form on a basic skill.

q: A competent performer of a basic push-up keeps the body in what position?
o: A straight line from head to heels
Head dropped with a rounded back
e: A straight body line shows correct form.

q: A coach tells a student to keep her elbows closer to her body during a row. Using the coach's comment to adjust is which type of feedback?
e: Feedback from another person is external.

q: You feel your lower back arching on an overhead press and fix your posture. This is an example of what?
o: Using internal feedback from body sensations
e: Body sensations provide internal feedback.

q: A workout alternates 30 seconds of hard effort with 30 seconds of rest for several rounds. What method is this?
e: Alternating work and rest periods is interval training.

q: A routine moves through six stations of different exercises with little rest between them. What method is this?
e: Circuit training rotates through stations.

q: Which clothing choice is best for a safe workout?
o: Supportive athletic shoes and clothing that allows free movement
e: Proper attire reduces injury risk.

q: Before using free weights, a student should do what with the equipment?
o: Inspect it and use collars and proper lifting technique
e: Safe handling prevents injury.

q: Which exercise technique is unsafe?
o: Bouncing hard at the bottom of a deep stretch
Slow controlled breathing during a lift
e: Ballistic bouncing can strain muscles and joints.

q: Holding your breath and locking the knees during a heavy lift can be harmful because it can do what?
o: Raise blood pressure and strain joints
e: Breath-holding and locked joints are risky.

q: On a hot, humid afternoon a runner sweats heavily. What is the best way to protect her?
o: Drink fluids before, during and after exercise
e: Hydration offsets fluid lost to sweat.

q: Which sign suggests a person may be becoming dehydrated during exercise?
o: Dizziness, dark urine and a dry mouth
e: Dehydration produces these signs.

q: Wellness includes more than the absence of disease. How does physical fitness relate to wellness?
o: Fitness supports physical, mental and social wellness
e: Fitness is one part of overall wellness.

q: A student who exercises regularly sleeps better and copes with stress more easily. This shows fitness contributes to what?
e: Fitness benefits several areas of wellness.

q: Which activity develops health-related fitness?
e: Sustained swimming builds cardiorespiratory endurance.

q: Which activity mainly develops muscular strength?
e: Resistance training builds strength.

q: To improve cardiorespiratory endurance, a person should train using which FITT idea?
o: Sustained activity at a raised heart rate several days a week
e: Endurance improves with regular sustained aerobic work.

q: To build muscular endurance, a good plan uses what?
o: Only static holds of one second
e: High reps with lighter loads build endurance.

q: Which pair includes one aerobic and one anaerobic activity?
e: Cycling is aerobic and heavy lifting is anaerobic.

q: A 100-meter sprint relies mostly on what kind of energy system?
e: Short bursts of maximum effort are anaerobic.

q: A student uses a fitness watch to check her heart rate zones while running. What is this technology used for?
e: Heart-rate tracking helps guide intensity.

q: Which technology tool best helps count steps across a week?
e: Pedometers and trackers count steps.

q: A personal fitness plan should include which parts?
o: Goals, activities for each fitness component, and a way to track progress
e: A plan sets goals, activities and tracking.

q: Which is a SMART goal for a fitness program?
o: Run a mile in under 10 minutes by the end of 8 weeks
e: SMART goals are specific, measurable and time-bound.

q: Agility, balance, coordination, power, reaction time and speed are examples of what?
e: These are the skill-related components.

q: A shuttle run is commonly used to measure which skill-related component?
e: Shuttle runs test quick changes of direction.

q: A sit-and-reach test measures which health-related component?
e: Sit-and-reach measures flexibility of the hamstrings and back.

q: A timed one-mile run is used to evaluate what?
e: Distance runs test aerobic capacity.

q: Regular physical activity is related to emotional health because it can do what?
e: Exercise supports mood and lowers stress.

q: Playing on a team can improve social health by doing what?
e: Team activity builds social skills.

q: A student who failed to run a mile in 12 minutes improves to 10 minutes after weeks of training. This shows that what?
o: Improvement is possible with appropriate practice
e: Practice produces improvement.

q: Which statement shows a growth mindset about fitness?
o: I was born weak and always will be
I can get stronger if I keep training consistently
e: A growth mindset values effort.

q: A teammate misses the winning shot. Which is the best response?
o: Encourage him and focus on learning from the play
e: Supportive responses handle failure well.

q: A conflict starts over a rule during a game. Which action resolves it best?
o: Calmly discuss the rule and agree on a solution
e: Calm communication resolves conflict.

q: A student wins a match and a rival loses. Which behavior shows good sportsmanship?
o: Shaking hands and acknowledging the opponent's effort
e: Respect is shown in success and defeat.

q: Accepting a performance limitation, such as a slower time, means doing what?
o: Working on it respectfully without putting yourself or others down
e: Healthy acceptance is paired with effort.

q: Spending several hours on screens instead of moving can affect social and emotional health by doing what?
e: Excess screen time can reduce activity and connection.

q: Using a fitness app to share goals with friends can have what positive effect?
o: It can increase motivation and support
e: Social features can motivate.

q: Why is sleep important for an athlete?
o: It allows the body to recover and supports performance
e: Recovery happens during sleep.

q: A student sleeping five hours a night before a meet will most likely experience what?
o: Slower reaction time and lower performance
e: Sleep loss hurts performance.

q: Which statement is a myth about physical activity?
o: Doing thousands of crunches burns the fat from your stomach only
e: Spot reduction is a myth.

q: Which is a nutrition myth?
o: Skipping meals is a healthy way to lose weight fast
e: Skipping meals is not a healthy strategy.

q: Eating a balanced meal with carbohydrates before long exercise helps because it does what?
e: Carbohydrates fuel exercise.

q: After a hard workout, a snack with protein and carbohydrates helps by doing what?
o: Supporting muscle repair and restoring energy
e: Protein and carbs aid recovery.

q: An athlete who trains hard every day with no rest days feels constantly tired and gets injured often. What is the likely cause?
e: Too much training without recovery causes problems.

q: Which is a sign of over training?
o: Persistent fatigue, declining performance and mood changes
e: These are common signs of over training.

q: An ad promises that a pill will melt away fat without exercise. How should a smart consumer respond?
o: Be skeptical and check the claim with a reliable source
e: Marketing claims need evidence.

q: Which source is the most reliable for fitness advice?
o: A certified trainer or a medical professional
e: Credentials indicate reliability.

q: Which combination best improves body composition?
e: Both exercise and nutrition affect body composition.

q: Body composition refers to the proportion of what in the body?
o: Fat mass compared with lean mass such as muscle and bone
e: It compares fat and lean tissue.
